title: The cake
logline: Friday. The last catering strip. The cake, drawn from memory, wrong: too many tiers. Gully says it's not a cake. Wood says it's what he remembers. Gully takes the pad and turns the page for him. The arc ends.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD drawing. The pad: a cake, six tiers, ornate, impossible.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man drawing an impossibly tall six-tier wedding cake on a pad at a bait-shop counter, a man in an apron, an old dog in a basket

panels.composition: The cake. Too tall. A figure on top — two figures — one drawn, one a blank shape.
props: the cake topper: one drawn, one blank

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a drawn wedding cake with two small figures on top, one rendered and one left as a blank outline
image.notes: The topper: Chloe drawn, Julian a blank shape. The strip's rule, on a cake.

balloons.text: It had three tiers. I saw the picture. She sent Maria the picture.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a stocky man in an apron disputing a drawing with a thin man on a stool

panels.composition: Gully reaching over. Taking the pad. Turning the page. A blank sheet. Handing it back. Wood looking at the blank. The dog's chin on the counter's edge.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a stocky man turning the page of a thin man's pad to a blank sheet and handing it back, an old dog's chin on the counter edge

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Six tiers remembered; three in the picture. 'Draw the dog.' The arc ends.
